newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA'S COSSACK RIG TO SHUT FOR REPAIRS IN '98.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA'S COSSACK RIG TO SHUT FOR REPAIRS IN '98.

text.p: The Cossack Pioneer oil platform offshore Western Australia will fully shut down for major repairs early next year, a spokesman for the operator, Woodside Petroleum Ltd, said on Tuesday.

A major repair programme on the platform, which is in the midst of a partial shut down of the gas export system to allow for interim repair work, would mainly involve work to the system, the spokesman told Reuters.
Problems with the gas export system have caused sporadic production dispruptions ever since the Cossack Pioneer was commissioned in November 1995.
Cossack Pioneer has been operating at an average rate of around 45,000 barrels a day since Sunday, when the interim work started, the spokesman said.
The current repair work is scheduled to last about two weeks, he said.
A more comprehensive repair programme next year will require a complete production shutdown, the spokesman said.
"We will look to fix the gas export system once and for all," he said.

The Cossack-Pioneer, which pumps crude oil and gas from the Wanaea and Cossack fields on the North West Shelf, had been producing about around 90,000 barrels a day prior to the latest repair work, he said.
The platform is designed to produce up to 115,000 barrels a day but has rarely operated at that level due to recurring technical problems.

Woodside is an equal one-seventh partner in the North West Shelf joint venture. The other partners are The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, Chevron Corp and Royal Dutch Shell Group.
